mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as elevated interest rates reduce the present value of future equity cash flows.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of observations with FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, or the Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and SPX 20d returns is positive over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 5.0%, it signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle that compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates a dual shock of labor market weakness and monetary tightening, which is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction term (UNRATE * FEDFUNDS) shows a positive correlation with SPX 20d returns over any 3-year rolling window, or the negative return signal occurs in less than 40% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by CPIAUCSL > 300 and GDPC1 > 22700), strong housing starts (HOUST) signal sustained consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 300 and GDPC1 > 22700, or the Rank IC between HOUST and SPX 20d returns is negative in the late-cycle regime.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as elevated joblessness signals economic weakness and reduced corporate earnings potential.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of observations with UNRATE > 4.5%, or the Rank IC between UNRATE and SPX 5d returns is positive over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.0%, it signals a tight labor market that supports strong consumer spending and corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0%, or the average return in such periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction term (HOUST * RSAFS) shows a negative correlation with SPX 5d returns over any 3-year rolling window, or the positive return signal occurs in less than 40% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply expansion regime (defined by INDPRO > 102), rising industrial production signals strong manufacturing activity and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO > 102, or the Rank IC between INDPRO and SPX 60d returns is negative in the supply expansion regime.
